reasons: Classification is correct: Article XII runs only from Licensee to Licensor and Article XIII(a) expressly disclaims any Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement claims, so there is no Vendor IP indemnity at all — squarely walk-away territory under INDEMN, not the fallback.

The inserted Licensor indemnity tracks the model language (IP infringement, breach of law, Licensor-caused data incidents, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) and adds the standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics; the 'Notwithstanding Article XIII or any other provision' opener is a sensible minimum addition to stop the liability exclusion from gutting the new indemnity.
Comment is accurate on the substance, concise, cites the playbook position and offers the 3x annual fees super-cap / customary-exclusions fallback in the required tone.

The failed 'minimal edit p0129' check is expected here — narrowing the Licensee indemnity necessarily rewrites subclauses (ii) and (iii); the changed-character ratio is not evidence of over-editing in this case.

Residual gap to raise in negotiation (not fatal): the redline leaves p0128's lead-in ('Licensee will be solely responsible for any commercial or legal liability ... as a result of Licensee's exercise of any of the license rights') and subclause (i) intact, which is still broader than the playbook's 'Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law' limit and could be read to circle IP-infringement exposure back to Licensee; the comment's claim that the Licensee indemnity was narrowed is therefore only partly delivered.
